protocol.py: 6 biology problems (1 error, 4 warnings, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 13.2 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 52:  p300.aspirate(vol_enzyme, tube_rack[positions[14]])  # enzyme tube
   At line 52 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 13.2 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul. A
   pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and
   the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells:
   tube C3 in slot 1.
   Affected: tube C3 in slot 1.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [972197d7917d]

2. WARNING ENZYME-BEFORE-DILUENT: An enzyme was added before the water: enzyme
   line 53:  p300.dispense(vol_enzyme, mix_tube)
   At line 53 the robot put enzyme into tube D6 in slot 1. Take tube D6 in slot 1: at that
   moment it held only 26.4 ul, all of it neat buffer, and the water came afterwards, at
   line 56, to make the 184.8 ul of water or buffer the reaction is built on. An enzyme is
   shipped in 50% glycerol and is meant to be the last thing into a reaction, after the
   water and the buffer have brought the well to the right dilution. Dropped into neat
   buffer or a dry well it meets many times the salt it should: a restriction enzyme then
   cuts at the wrong places (star activity) and a polymerase starts on mis-primed template.
   Affected: tube D6 in slot 1.
   Fix: Reorder the additions to tube D6 in slot 1: water and buffer first, then the sample,
   then enzyme last. Or make a master mix of water, buffer and enzyme in one tube, mix it,
   and hand it out.
   Source: Thermo Fisher: restriction enzyme key considerations (the enzyme is the final
   component)
           https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/life-science/cloning/cloning-learning-center/invitrogen-school-of-molecular-biology/molecular-cloning/restriction-enzymes/restriction-enzyme-key-considerations.html
   Source: Promega: restriction enzyme resource (add the enzyme last; glycerol and star
   activity)
           https://www.promega.com/resources/guides/nucleic-acid-analysis/restriction-enzyme-resource/
   Source: NEB: Q5 High-Fidelity PCR kit manual (add the polymerase last)
           https://www.neb.com/-/media/nebus/files/manuals/manuale0555.pdf
   Source: Qiagen: critical factors for successful real-time PCR (order of addition)
           https://www.gene-quantification.de/qiagen-qpcr-sample-assay-tech-guide-2010.pdf
   [f30ad9d1d3e3]

3. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (tube C1 in slot 1)
   line 55:  p300.aspirate(vol_water, tube_rack[positions[12]])   # water tube
   At line 55 the tip went into water (tube C1 in slot 1) while it still carried buffer
   (tube C2 in slot 1) and enzyme (tube C3 in slot 1) from an earlier step. A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from it again, so
   this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next
   run.
   Affected: tube C1 in slot 1.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 55 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [c984c30e6c78]

4. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 12 wells: 2 × 10 ul in 15 ul
   line 66:  p20.mix(2, 10, plate[well])
   At line 66 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 2 with 2
   strokes of 10 ul in a well holding 15 ul (this line did it 12 times). 2 strokes of 10 ul
   move 1.33 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the mixing
   work). Fewer than 3 strokes do not mix a well. Integra draws over 80% of the well five
   times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated, and in a dilution series every later step inherits the
   error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2 and 4 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (12 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 12,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [c47e5152b5b8]

   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
